title: Deploy sampled-request-aware circuit breaker + automated hotpatch flow to arrest hosted API 5xx/retry spirals
creator: Amit Rao
description: Summary: During several recent customer escalations we saw large buckets of retries cause short-lived 5xx waves driven by long-tail timeouts and edge-side request fanout. This ticket implements two coordinated mitigations: (1) a lightweight sampled-request circuit breaker that trips based on a sampled signal stream (reduces noisy metrics from retries and avoids punishing single long-lived requests) and (2) an automated hotpatch build + safe-deploy flow in the control plane so SREs can push a minimal runtime patch (circuit config + backoff overrides) with canned rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Circuit breaker accepts a dynamic sampling rate and calculates a trip score using sampled latencies + error counts (P95 latency and 5xx ratio) per AZ and host
When trip score exceeds threshold for 30s, incoming sampled requests are fast-failed with a deterministic HTTP 503 and a Retry-After header; non-sampled requests continue to be processed
Hotpatch flow packages the change into a signed runtime bundle; canary rollout to 5% of hosts with automated health checks and a 3-minute safe-rollback window
Console exposes a one-click emergency-revert that rolls back the hotpatch and surfaces the sampling rate + trip threshold used
End-to-end test harness that can simulate retry storms and assert that tail latency and 5xx counts fall by >= 60% within 2 minutes of circuit activation
notes: Rationale: full host-wide circuit breakers require opaque global signals and have caused customer-visible outages in the past. Sampling reduces false positives and limits blast radius.
We intentionally fast-fail sampled requests so callers see early deterministic errors and apply client-side exponential backoff rather than continuing to amplify the runtime load.
This approach complements existing per-tenant shaping and admission controls rather than replacing them.
We will limit sampled-failure codepath to hosted for the initial launch; Dedicated and Private follow-ups are tracked as sub-issues (see dependencies).
implementation_plan: Design: define sampled signal (1% base, up to 10% during elevated signals) and trip scoring function — ENG/arch RFC link: <confluence>/rfc/sampled-circuit-breaker (placeholder)
Runtime: add lightweight sampler and scoring window in frontdoor proxy (C++, ~400 LOC change). Expose config via control plane config API.
Control plane: implement hotpatch builder that produces signed manifests + rollout policy (canary %, health checks, rollback TTL).
Console: add an emergency hotpatch modal showing sampling rate, trip score graph, and one-click rollback. UX spec: <drive>/drafts/hotpatch-ui-v1 (placeholder)
Observability: add dedicated metrics: sampled_requests_total, sampled_trip_score, sampled_fastfail_rate; add dashboard and an alert when sampled_trip_score >= warning threshold
E2E test: synthetic load generator that reproduces retry amplification and verifies mitigation impact
Runbook: write an incident runbook for on-call to toggle sampling or kick hotpatch rollback
progress_log: 2026-02-18 - Amit Rao created the ticket after post-incident review of INC-2026-02-12. Initial design sketched in RFC.
2026-02-25 - Spike complete: implemented local sampler prototype and load-tested in dev cluster. Observed 55% reduction in tail 5xx under synthetic retry workload (Diego Alvarez).
2026-03-03 - Control plane hotpatch builder prototype merged to feature branch (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2129).
2026-03-08 - Telemetry schema added: sampled_trip_score metric emitted from proxy (Claire Chen).
2026-03-12 - Canaries scheduled: 5% rollout plan drafted. QA testcases for safe-rollback created.
2026-03-15 - Began staging canary rollout to internal staging-hosted pool. Observability dashboard updated; no customer-facing regressions so far.
review_feedback: PM (Diego Alvarez): ensure customer comms template is ready if we use sampled fast-fail (customers may see 503s briefly).
Security (Nina Patel): hotpatch manifest must be signed and audit-logged. Added to control plane acceptance criteria.
SRE (Ethan Brooks): add per-AZ trip thresholds to avoid cross-AZ cascading; recommend 30s stabilization window. Incorporated.
SDK team (Olga Ivanov): add guidance to SDK retry policy to respect Retry-After header; requested a change in SDKs after rollout.
open_questions: What default client-facing status code is best — 503 (temporarily overloaded) vs 429 (too many requests)? Need legal/SLAs input.
Should we serve a diagnostic header that indicates sampling id so customers can map observed 503s to our sampled policy? Privacy review required.
Target sampling strategy during a major sustained incident: do we scale sampling linearly with trip score or use step-ups to avoid oscillation?
postmortem_actions: Add automated detection for transient retry storms to trigger suggested sampling config in console
Document customer-facing comms template and SDK guidance updates
Plan Dedicated/Private adaptation: map sampling config to tenant-level roles and allow tenant opt-out
